timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I'm Boven, thank you for being a part of the Teddy Jury this year. Can you start by giving
a brief introduction of yourself and your work? Hello my name is Bo Bo Van from China, but
recently living in Berlin. I am a committee member of the Beijing Queer Film Festival. I have
been working for it since 2007 and I'm also a filmmaker. Previously made a lot of documentary
featuring LGBT families in China, now in Berlin doing more fictional and experimental
rock movies. And that your previous films that you made I think they have been used as
sort of quite an activist purpose within China. I wondered if you think queer film can and
should be used for activism. I think film is definitely one of the very important
tools for communication. So my understanding about film in the beginning was something able
to change the society. Of course I was too naive, the world wouldn't be changed just
by film. So I would say activism in the country is one of the way of filmmaking. So that
is why also right now I am exploring more diverse ways of filmmaking and more contribution
to the queer film culture and society. And we have one queer film from China this year.
And I wanted to just generally what the queer film scene is like in China. Is there an issue
with censorship at all? Yeah, unfortunately because of the censorship and no queer film
will be able to show on the big screen in China. So they have to work on the very bad situation.
There is no money and very few people could work on it. I stayed for the Q&A for a dark
working to the moon yesterday. I was very impressed how much effect that the director had
made. And this is not the only case I can see in China any director want to feature this
topic. They have to work 100 times more than people from doing other issues. So I really
appreciate it. And I am calling Chinese government to change the censorship system and made
LGBT topic to be able to be featuring film and to reach bigger audience.
How do you think your background will help you with making a decision this year for the

Oh god. I really appreciate that the tele-award organizer would invite people from different

youtube_description:
Hannah Congdon in conversation with TEDDY Jury member Popo Fan.

Born in 1985, Popo Fan is a Chinese queer filmmaker, activist and writer. In 2007, Fan published his first book on queer films before he graduated from Beijing Film Academy. From 2009 to 2016, he made a strong impact on Chinese society with a documentary trilogy focusing on LGBTQI* families in China. Fan won a lawsuit against the government after his film Mama Rainbow had been taken off the internet, a landmark event in fighting against state censorship in China. 
Fan has served as an organizer for the Beijing Queer Film Festival for more than a decade; he also founded the Queer University Video Training Camp in China. Currently he lives in Berlin developing his feature debut, at the same time writing for media such as Vice China. Among various achievements, Fan received the Hong Kong Lesbian and Gay Film Festival’s Prism Award in 2011 and participated in Berlinale Talents in 2017.
